full_judgment: 2. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant submits that since a civil suit is pending, all the reliefs could be had in that suit, the drawing up of criminal proceeding will bring about a conflict of jurisdiction between civil and criminal Courts and it might lead to conflicting judgments. It appears that the suit is for specific performance of contract and so unless a decree on the contract is given and is completed by execution of the Kabala, no title accrues in favour of the purchaser and hence the question of possession becomes secondary. In a suit of this nature possession is not linked up with the main claim of the suit, as the title does not accrue on the passing of the decree. It, however, appears that the plaintiffs of the Title Suit who are the first party to the criminal proceeding have also claimed for permanent injunction on the assertion that they got possession on the execution of the contract for sale of the land. It is also to be remembered that the prayer or injunction regarding possession of the land was not granted, through there is no specific refusal either. In such circumstances, if there is a serious apprehension of breach of peace which is apparent from the record, the exercise of the Magistrate's jurisdiction is called for. We think that the ends of justice would be met if the Magistrate is directed not to pass any final order regarding possession till the disposal of the suit by the trial court.
